title: Type 2 Diabetes & Chronic Kidney Disease

patient.name: John Doe

clinicalInfo.primaryDiagnosis: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Chronic Kidney Disease Stage 3b

patient.dietaryHistory: 24-hour dietary recall indicates high sodium intake (~3,800mg/day), moderate animal protein (1.2g/kg), frequent high-glycemic carbohydrates, and inadequate soluble fiber. Fluid intake approx 1,500ml.

dietaryRecommendations: Moderate protein restriction: 0.6 - 0.8 g/kg body weight/day to slow renal decline.
Sodium restriction: < 2,000 mg/day to control blood pressure and proteinuria.
Consistent carbohydrate counting: 45-60g per meal with low glycemic index choices.
Monitor dietary potassium and phosphorus: limit high-phosphorus additives and processed meats.
Adequate hydration: 1.8 - 2.0 L/day unless volume overloaded.

title: Celiac Disease in Adolescence with Malabsorption

patient.name: Maya Patel

medications: Ferrous Sulfate 325mg daily with Vitamin C

patient.dietaryHistory: Reports chronic abdominal bloating, fatigue, and unintentional weight loss over 8 months following school canteen meals with wheat flour.

dietaryRecommendations: Strict lifelong gluten-free diet (zero wheat, barley, rye, or contaminated oats).
Temporary low-lactose diet until intestinal villous atrophy recovers.
Iron and Vitamin D supplementation coupled with vitamin C-rich foods.
Calorie-dense, nutrient-rich meals to promote catch-up growth.

title: Marathon Training Nutrition & Glycogen Periodization

patient.name: Alex Carter
patient.dietaryHistory: Under-fueling on long run days (consuming only water for 2.5 hour runs). Post-workout protein intake delayed > 3 hours.

dietaryRecommendations: Carbohydrate periodization: 7-10 g/kg/day during heavy training cycles.
Intra-workout fueling: 30-60 g/hour of multiple transportable carbohydrates (glucose:fructose 2:1).
Electrolyte hydration plan: 400-800 ml/hr fluid with 500-700 mg/L sodium.
Post-exercise recovery: 1.0-1.2 g/kg carbohydrates + 0.3 g/kg high-quality protein within 45 minutes.
